LiquidLyf is a community tool that helps people find voluntary blood donors. It is not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any medical condition.

LiquidLyf does not collect, test, store, or supply blood, and does not verify donors' health or identity. Blood must be donated only at a licensed hospital or blood transfusion centre, where it will be screened.

Always consult a doctor or other qualified healthcare professional for medical advice. Never pay or accept money for blood. In an emergency, call 999.
Who gets alerted, and when your number is shared
When someone posts a blood request, LiquidLyf alerts suitable donors nearby, nearest first. Nobody is alerted more than they need to be.
Donors who are listed, ready to donate and able to donate now: 18 to 60 years old, with at least 4 months since their last donation, and a blood group the patient can receive.

Alerts start in the hospital\'s upazila. If not enough donors offer, they widen step by step: other suitable blood groups nearby (if the requester accepts them), then the whole district, then the neighbouring districts. Rh-negative requests start with the district, then the whole division. When the offers cover the units needed, the next step waits.
You get at most two alerts for the same request: when it\'s posted, and once more if it\'s still needed. Each person can send alerts for only a few requests a day.
A requester can also search listed donors by blood group and area, and ask one to donate. Each person can ask only a limited number of donors a day.

Your phone number is never listed. It\'s shared with a requester only when you offer to donate on their request. A request\'s contact details are shown only to donors who offered, and they\'re hidden again if the offer is withdrawn or declined.
Turn off \"Ready to donate\" to pause alerts, or stop being listed in Settings → Privacy. After you donate, alerts stop by themselves until you can donate again.
